title: Volatile food trade policy threatens biodiversity | Science
content: International trade has benefited food security and biodiversity by leveraging the comparative advantages of countries (1), but the role of international trade stability in safeguarding ecosystems is often overlooked. Volatile food trade policies such as trade bans in response to the COVID-19 pandemic (2), export restrictions related to the Russia’s invasion of Ukraine (3), and import tariffs imposed by the Trump administration (4) have reshaped the food supply chain, leading to cascading effects on biodiversity loss through agricultural production (5), land use change (6), and natural resource use (7). Prioritizing trade policy stability and clarifying its connection to biodiversity conservation can offer a pathway toward improving both food security and ecological resilience.
